title: Kubelet heartbeat pipeline latency investigation notes
content:
Summary:

During a partial degradation window on 2024-11-03 (08:42–11:20 UTC) we observed persistent kubelet heartbeat processing latency on a subset of GPU node pools in us-west-2. Symptoms: pods stuck in Pending for 30–120s, sporadic node NotReady flaps, and an increased eviction rate for pods with local ephemeral storage (emptyDir). Overall platform impact: ~4% of clusters experienced user-facing request timeouts for inference endpoints that required scheduling on new pods (scale-up path).

Why this doc exists (notes-to-self tone):
- Capture what triggered the alarm (heartbeat pipeline, not network).
- Track commands/metrics that helped triage.
- Draft a short runbook addition for future on-call responders.
- Record open follow-ups for eng infra.

Detection & Alerting:
- Alert SRE: node-heartbeat-latency > 300ms sustained for > 5m (fired 08:46 UTC).
- Prometheus panels: kubelet_heartbeat_processing_seconds_bucket and kubelet_runtime_operations_latency spiked across ~12 nodes in the gpu-nv4-pool-2 group.
- Pager data: increased API Server 429s for pod creation (backpressure) and kube-scheduler requeue rate increased by ~7x.

Initial observations (what we saw):
- Affected nodes: 12/240 on cluster-prod-usw2-gpu-*.
- Node metric pattern: CPU steal % rose from 2% -> 18% on affected nodes; iowait spiked to 9–12%.
- kubelet logs: repeated timestamps showing long loop durations in "syncPodLoop" and warnings about "heartbeat handler took X ms".
- dmesg: occasional kernel slab/shrinker messages and journal shows repeated fsync latency on /var/lib/kubelet.
- Network: CNI metrics (calico) looked normal; no obvious packet loss.

Hypothesis (first-pass):
- Root contributor is a local I/O hotspot on affected nodes causing kubelet internal queues (heartbeat & pod worker) to stall. Likely caused by a mix of: heavy ephemeral I/O from inference container caching, noisy local backup job, and aggressive kubelet eviction thresholds triggering a feedback loop.

Quick timeline (UTC):
- 08:42: first user report (inference timeout).
- 08:46: SRE alert fired (heartbeat latency).
- 08:50: On-call pulled metrics; confirmed 12 nodes showing elevated loop times.
- 08:58: We SSH'd a sample node (gpu-23) and saw nontrivial journald growth and a large number (~120k) of inodes in /var/lib/kubelet/pods (emptyDir churn).
- 09:12: Scaled down a single suspected noisy daemonset (local-cache-sync) as mitigation on two nodes -> immediate drop in iowait and heartbeat latency on those nodes within 90s.
- 09:40: Rolling cordon/drain of 4 most affected nodes to relieve pressure; scheduling latencies normalized cluster-wide by ~10:55.

Commands & checks used (copied here for runbook portability):
- kubectl top node gpu-23 --use-protocol-buffers
- ssh gpu-23 "sudo iotop -b -o -P -n 5"
- journalctl -u kubelet -o short-iso | sed -n '1,200p'
- sudo du -sh /var/lib/kubelet/* | sort -h
- sudo ss -nptu | grep kubelet
- kubectl get events --all-namespaces --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Pod | grep -i eviction

Why the DS scale-down helped (evidence):
- The local-cache-sync daemonset was performing frequent fsyncs to emptyDir mounts every ~10s for persistence window reasons. On nodes with many local volumes (memmapped model caches) this produced heavy fsync+write amplification which increased iowait and blocked kubelet disk-related syscalls.
- After stopping the DS, fsync counts dropped from ~300/s -> <20/s observed via perf counters; kubelet loop latency returned to baseline.

Root cause analysis (current best understanding):
- Primary: High local fsync/write amplification from an internal daemonset targeting model-cache directories on nodes with slower local NVMe firmware behavior (some older firmware versions found on a subset of GPU SKUs).
- Secondary: Kubelet eviction thresholds for imagefs/ephemeral-storage are configured aggressively; during sustained iowait the eviction manager got slower to react which caused pod churn, increasing emptyDir churn and making the pressure worse (feedback loop).
- Tertiary: Scheduler requeue/backpressure compounded user-facing latencies because API server started responding with 429s under high create/delete churn.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Scaled down local-cache-sync daemonset (temporary) on affected pools at 09:12.
- Cordoned and drained 4 worst nodes (09:40) to give time for kubelet to reconcile volumes and allow normal scheduling on other nodes.
- Increased imagefs eviction threshold by 5% on the cluster as a temporary safety margin (applied via kops patch; risk: longer time to reclaim disk in genuine OOM/disk-full cases).
- Added a temporary Prometheus alert to watch for fsync rate > 100/s per node.

Longer-term remediation (action items):
- Action A (Infra): Audit NVMe firmware across GPU SKUs and roll firmware update where vendor fixes reduce write latency. Owner: Ethan Zhao. ETA: 3 weeks.
- Action B (SRE/Infra): Add a kubelet config knob and gate to surface fsync/write syscall rate to node exporter; add alert runbook mapping. Owner: Priya Nair. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Action C (Solutions/Eng): Update local-cache-sync to batch writes and reduce fsync frequency; add backoff on heavy I/O signals. Owner: Jonah Rivera (team: solutions). ETA: 2 sprints.
- Action D (SRE): Revisit eviction thresholds and add hysteresis to eviction manager to avoid tight feedback loops; prototype in staging. Owner: Maya Chen & SRE. ETA: 4 weeks.
- Action E (Scheduler): Add a short-term mitigation to reduce API server requeues by temporarily increasing scheduler burst quota under high churn. Owner: Platform Eng. ETA: 1 week.

Proposed runbook fragment (for incident responder):
- Alert: node-heartbeat-latency > 300ms for > 5m.
- Step 1: Identify top-10 nodes by kubelet loop latency: run PromQL: topk(10, increase(kubelet_sync_pod_loop_duration_seconds_sum[5m]) / increase(kubelet_sync_pod_loop_duration_seconds_count[5m]))
- Step 2: SSH to one affected node. Check: iotop, vmstat 1 5, dstat, journalctl -u kubelet. Look specifically for high fsync counts and journald growth.
- Step 3: If high fsync/writes, find any active DaemonSets writing to /var/lib/kubelet or emptyDir mounts: kubectl get ds --all-namespaces -o wide and check pod command args.
- Step 4: If suspected DS, scale down to 0 on one node first (kubectl -n X scale ds Y --replicas=0 --dry-run=client then patch nodeSelector) and observe iowait; if improvement, roll out scaledown across affected pool.
- Step 5: If node is irrecoverable, cordon+drain and replace.
- Step 6: Post-mortem: capture perf counters (fsync_count), nvme logs, kubelet metrics and link to JIRA ticket.

Unresolved questions / research items (notes):
- Why did kubelet eviction manager not trigger sooner? Did the eviction controller rely on wall-clock checks blocked by fsyncs? Need to instrument the eviction manager’s internal timing in kubelet logs.
- Could we implement an adaptive per-node fsync rate limit at the daemonset level as a short stop-gap? (This would be a band-aid.)
- Are certain NVMe firmware versions correlated 1:1 with the degraded behavior? We saw a strong correlation but need vendor confirmation.

Post-incident notes & comms:
- Customer-facing summary prepared for CS describing brief scheduling delays during the window; no model inference data lost, only scheduling latency impacts during scale-up. Draft in CS: https://docs.google.com/document/d/summary-draft (internal).
- Internal postmortem assigned: SRE-4794. Target postmortem in 2 weeks with RCA and follow-ups closed.

Appendix (raw snippets & observations):
- kubelet log snippet: "W1103 08:49:21.123 kubelet_manager.go:280] heartbeat handler took 1123ms"
- iostat on gpu-23: avgqu-sz jumped to 21; await to 312ms for /dev/nvme0n1
- perf trace: fsync() frequency correlated to container ID abc123 (~270/s)

Notes to self:
- Keep the runbook short and prescriptive. The most important first step is to check fsync/write rate and local daemonsets writing to emptyDir.
- Consider adding a small diagnostic script that can be run from SRE workstation to snapshot node state (iotop, vmstat, du /var/lib/kubelet, kernel slab stats). Put this under helpers/node-snapshot in repo.

Open action items (quick list):
- [ ] Create SRE-4794 and attach graphs/logs (owner: Maya Chen)
- [ ] Firmware audit – start vendor engagement (owner: Ethan Zhao)
- [ ] Implement node exporter fsync metric (owner: Priya Nair)
- [ ] Patch local-cache-sync to reduce fsyncs (owner: Jonah Rivera)
- [ ] Adjust kubelet eviction hysteresis prototype (owner: Maya Chen)

If you're the on-call: first check the fsync rate on the node and the presence of any local daemonsets that could be writing intensively. If you can't find a quick mitigation, cordon & drain the node to stop user impact and escalate to infra for a hardware/firmware look.

End of notes.
